title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.10
exact_target: Can every finite group be presented so that removal of any single relation makes the resulting group infinite?

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, \emph{UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems}, record 2519 (KOU-21.10). CC BY 4.0.

Y. Barnea, Problem 21.10, in E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), \emph{The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory}, 21st edition, arXiv:1401.0300v48 (6 October 2026). This version records an affirmative answer; the displayed question is the historically registered target.

Marc Lackenby, \emph{Every finite group admits a just finite presentation}, arXiv:2605.10402v1 (2026), Introduction and Theorem 1. The theorem gives an affirmative answer with finite generating and relator sets.
